findings.title: Primary submit action is a clickable div
findings.explanation: The 'Sign up' action is a div with onClick and no role, tabIndex or key handler. Keyboard and assistive-technology users cannot focus or activate it, so the signup form cannot be submitted by keyboard. It is also not a submit button, so Enter in the input does not submit via a button.
findings.suggested_fix: Use <button type="submit">Sign up</button> and drop the onClick, letting the form's onSubmit handle submission.

findings.title: Email input has no programmatic label
findings.explanation: The input relies on placeholder only, with no label, aria-label or aria-labelledby. Screen readers cannot reliably identify the field, and the hint disappears on typing. This is a main-flow form field.
findings.suggested_fix: Add <label htmlFor="email">Email</label> and id="email" on the input (or an aria-label).

findings.title: Custom modal has no dialog semantics or focus management
findings.explanation: The modal is plain divs with no role="dialog", aria-modal, accessible name, initial focus, focus trap, Escape-to-close or focus return, and no accessible dialog library is imported. Keyboard focus stays behind the overlay and users cannot dismiss it. Severity assumes the modal blocks a main flow (usage not seen in this project).
findings.suggested_fix: Use native <dialog> with showModal() or an accessible library (Radix Dialog, Headless UI, React Aria); otherwise add role="dialog", aria-modal="true", aria-labelledby, move focus in on open, trap Tab, close on Escape and restore focus on close.

findings.title: Avatar image has no alt attribute
findings.explanation: The img has no alt attribute, so screen readers may announce the file URL. Pass an alt prop for informative avatars, or alt="" if decorative.
findings.suggested_fix: Accept an alt prop (e.g. the user's name) and render , using alt="" when the avatar is decorative.

limitations: Only three source files were present; no Modal, Avatar or SignupForm call sites were visible, so real-world usage and severity in context could not be verified.
Color contrast, focus appearance and actual screen-reader output cannot be verified from source.
No ESLint config was present, so eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y does not appear to be configured.
Listing was done with read-only shell find because Glob/Grep were not used.
